Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: Trigger case (absolutive) overtly marked throughout: pronouns have dedicated trigger forms (ako, ka, siya); NPs take an/su.
curated_comment: Albay Bikol (alba1269, ISO bhk, Austronesian, Philippines) is a Philippine-type ergative language per Fincke (2002). The non-trigger case (ERG) marks A; S and P share the trigger case (ABS). All base values confirmed correct. GB409_15=1 confirmed with direct evidence: experiencers of perception and cognition (na-iling 'see', ma-mati' 'hear') take ERG case (pp.82-83). GB409_16=0 (topical A takes ABS in the classic Philippine pivot). GB409_22=1: pag-clauses show split intransitivity where S takes ERG (p.113, ex.142). GB409_23=1: ERG markers double as genitive (p.99). GB409_19 and GB409_24 remain '?' (no inanimate A examples; no INST/COM data in source). Glottocode alba1269 is correct.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comment: Pronoun table (p.81, Fig.11) shows clear ABS/ERG distinction for all persons. 1sg: ako (T) vs. ko (ERG).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comment: 2sg: ka/ika (T) vs. mo (ERG). Clear ABS/ERG distinction.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comment: 3sg: siya (T) vs. niya (ERG). Clear ABS/ERG distinction.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comment: Personal names take si (T) vs. ni (ERG); full NPs take an/su (T) vs. ki/kan (non-trigger/ERG).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comment: Imperfective (CV- reduplication) and perfective (-in-, pig-) both show consistent ERG alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comment: Perfective clauses consistently show ERG alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comment: ERG alignment maintained in past-tense ('commenced tense') constructions.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comment: ERG alignment maintained in non-past ('non-commenced tense') constructions.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
Comment: All declarative/indicative clauses show ERG alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comment: Non-indicative moods (commands, irrealis) maintain ERG alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
Comment: Realis clauses maintain ERG alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comment: Irrealis (negation, conditionals with kon, past counterfactuals) maintain ERG alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comment: Canonical agentive A consistently marked with ERG ko/ni/kan.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comment: Perceptual and cognitive experiencers also take ERG: na-iling ko ito 'I saw that' (p.82-83, ex.76); ma-ma-mati' ito ni Andres 'Andres will hear that' (ex.84). Non-agentive A takes ERG.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comment: Topical/trigger argument is always in ABS (trigger case); A is always non-trigger/ERG. GB409_16=0 is the canonical Philippine-type pattern.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comment: All non-topical A arguments are ERG; every transitive example shows this pattern.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comment: Animate A (human agents and experiencers) consistently take ERG.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comment: No examples of inanimate A in transitive clauses in this source; value unresolvable.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comment: Main clauses show ERG alignment throughout.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comment: Subordinate/complement/relative clauses preserve ERG marking (pp.68, 110).

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comment: In conditional pag-clauses (p.113, ex.142), S argument takes ERG instead of expected ABS. This split intransitivity is variably present (Fincke qualifies optionality).

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comment: ERG marker (ko/ni/kan) also marks possession (p.99: su kamot ko 'my hand'; ni Mamay as possessor). Canonical Philippine ERG=GEN syncretism.

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comment: Source does not identify an instrumental case or show ERG markers glossed as instrumental; value unresolvable.
